title: U.S. House · California's 8th District
area: Covers part of the Sacramento Valley and North Bay, including Fairfield, Vallejo and Richmond, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, John Garamendi (D) placed first with 54.4% (97,155 votes) and Rudy Recile (R) placed second with 27.8% (49,599 votes) out of 178,561 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: John Garamendi
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with a majority of votes cast

summary.text: John Garamendi previously served as California's Insurance Commissioner for eight years and as Deputy Secretary of the U.S. Department of the Interior. He serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure and Armed Services committees.

background.text: Born in Camp Blanding, Florida; earned a B.A. from UC Berkeley in 1966 and an M.B.A. from Harvard University in 1970.
Served in the U.S. Peace Corps and worked as a businessman and rancher; served as Deputy Secretary of the U.S. Department of the Interior.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

priorities.text: Past campaign materials describe support for investment in transportation, clean technology, education and research, and for extending tax savings to middle-class families and small businesses.

positions.summary: Says he supports expanding the background check system and keeping weapons of war out of communities, and that he introduced California's assault weapons ban as a state senator.
positions.quote: We must prevent these massacres from happening by instituting common-sense reforms, like expanding our background check system and preventing dangerous weapons from ending up in the wrong hands.

positions.summary: Says he supports a woman's fundamental right to choose and is a member of the Pro-Choice Caucus.
positions.quote: I fervently support a woman’s fundamental right to choose.

positions.summary: Says he supports increased investment in clean, renewable energy and a transition away from fossil fuels, with support for fossil fuel workers.
positions.quote: We cannot combat climate change without increasing investments in clean, renewable energy.

positions.summary: Introduced his own Iran war powers resolution and issued a statement welcoming House passage of the Iran War Powers Resolution, saying only Congress can declare war.
positions.quote: Today’s vote reaffirms the Constitutional principle that only Congress can declare war.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, including its Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, Highways and Transit, and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves on the House Committee on Armed Services, including its Readiness and Strategic Forces subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.name: Rudy Recile
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: Retired U.S. Army Major; small business owner

summary.text: Rudy Recile is a retired U.S. Army Major with over 26 years of military service and a former U.S. Department of Agriculture employee who has lived in Solano County for 18 years.

background.text: Born in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada; served in the U.S. Army from 1988 to 2014.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Eastern Illinois University in 1995 and a graduate degree from National Graduate School in 2005.

Worked as a U.S. Department of Agriculture employee and owns a small web design company; is affiliated with Veterans of Foreign Wars Post 2333, the National Rifle Association, and Solano and Yolo County Republican Party committees.

priorities.text: Lists platform issues including energy independence, support for the Bill of Rights, government spending accountability, public safety, support for veterans, California water issues, and education.
priorities.quote: My platform issues include energy independence, supporting the Bill of Rights, tax dollars accountability, public safety, supporting veterans, California's water issues and quality education.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page criticizes power plant shutdowns by those who dislike carbon fuels, calls wind and solar unreliable, and favors more oil exploration and nuclear energy.
positions.quote: Green power only works when the sun is shining or wind is blowing.

researchNotes: Neither candidate has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Garamendi's priorities and healthcare position are drawn from an older (2016) campaign-website excerpt reproduced on Ballotpedia, since no current 2026 issue statement was found; his committee record is current. Recile's issue positions were not detailed on his campaign homepage beyond the listed platform topics, so specific stances were not documented.
